SocialPage.lead: Outdoormídia understands that market leadership is not built on innovation, technology and urban presence alone. It is also sustained through clear values, consistency and institutional responsibility.
SocialPage.eticosP1: Outdoormídia is part of Corajosamente Éticos, a global movement that promotes personal and professional ethics as the basis of social change, confronting the culture of corruption and standing for a fair market.
SocialPage.eticosP2: It is not a one-off action or an institutional campaign. It is a continuous commitment to integrity and consistency in internal and external relationships, built into our organisational culture and guiding decisions, behaviour and initiatives.
SocialPage.eticosP3: For anyone buying outdoor media, that has a practical effect: the same standard we apply internally is the one that governs the contract, the negotiation and what we promise on the street.
SocialPage.eticosAlt: The seal of the Corajosamente Éticos movement
SocialPage.lojaAlt: Shelves at Loja OM do Bem, with tote bags made from reused billboard vinyl
SocialPage.lojaH2: The vinyl that comes off the face becomes income.
SocialPage.lojaP1: Loja OM do Bem is the practical initiative within Corajosamente Éticos. It gives form to Outdoormídia’s commitment to social responsibility, the circular economy and internal engagement.
SocialPage.lojaP2: We donate, at no cost, the advertising vinyl that has completed its display cycle. Trained seamstresses turn the material into tote bags and other products, generating income and taking waste out of circulation. Those items are sold at the shop, alongside snacks and rotating products.
SocialPage.lojaP3: All the profit goes in full to the NGO Caminho do Renascer.
SocialPage.renascerAlt: Children supported by the NGO Caminho do Renascer
SocialPage.renascerP1: Founded in 2009 by volunteers from the community itself, Caminho do Renascer supports children, adolescents and families in vulnerable situations in the Campo Comprido neighbourhood of Curitiba.
SocialPage.renascerP2: Many of those families live in precarious conditions in the protected area of the Barigui river basin, without adequate infrastructure and exposed to the risk of flooding and poor sanitation, with public services still patchy. That is where the shop’s proceeds arrive.
SocialPage.tampinhasAlt: Colourful plastic bottle caps collected at Outdoormídia’s reception
SocialPage.tampinhasP1: The Tampinha Solidária Campaign, run by the Associação das Acácias da Emiliano Perneta (AAEP), turns plastic caps into geriatric diapers for care homes in need.
SocialPage.tampinhasP2: Outdoormídia supports the initiative through cap donations from employees, combining sustainability and solidarity. Every 1 kg of donated caps becomes one diaper, offering care and dignity to those who need it most.
SocialPage.lojaNota: Loja OM do Bem is not a commercial product or a media platform. It is not part of the OOH portfolio. It is an initiative of corporate culture and ethics.
SocialPage.lojaCta: See the full life cycle of the vinyl
SocialPage.anunciandoP1: Anunciando o Bem turns media into direct social impact: a panel dedicated exclusively to the cause, with all its revenue going to those who need it most.
SocialPage.anunciandoP2: One hundred percent of the value generated by campaigns on this panel goes to the NGO Caminho do Renascer, which supports children, adolescents and families in vulnerable situations in Curitiba.
SocialPage.anunciandoP3: For the advertiser, it is the chance to communicate a product with purpose: presence that also sustains a real cause.
SocialPage.anunciandoStatTexto: Between bonuses, direct billing and trade deals converted into food for the NGO.
SocialPage.redeTitulo: The network at the service of the city
SocialPage.redeLead: The future of OOH will not be defined by the ability to generate visibility. It will be defined by the ability to generate value.
SocialPage.regAlt: A post at the Batel Convenience Square with a monitoring camera and a Muralha Digital emergency button
SocialPage.regP1: Batel Convenience Square. The first outdoor media asset connected to Curitiba’s Muralha Digital, the city’s monitoring and urban intelligence system.
SocialPage.regP2: The structure keeps doing its job of connecting brands and people, but it now also contributes to public safety and to the quality of urban space. It combines monitoring integrated into the Muralha Digital with an emergency button installed to provide help in vulnerable situations, in one of the most used community spaces in the city.
SocialPage.regP3: We are pioneers in integrating outdoor media and urban safety in Curitiba. In a market discussing ESG and smart cities, this is the difference between occupying a space and improving a space.
SocialPage.regP4: For the advertiser, it is the chance to be on a structure the city recognises as useful. Urban presence is also urban responsibility, and the best communication is the kind that leaves a legacy.

AmbientalPage.lead: Occupying the city for 67 years creates an obligation towards it. Our answer is not a report: it is squares delivered, living panels and vinyl that comes back as a product. Outdoor media that gives back, in practice, to the space it occupies.
AmbientalPage.realidadeLead: We are not talking about environmental intentions. We are talking about structures delivered, with an address, maintenance on us and daily public use. Every project below is an outdoor media asset the city uses even when it is not looking at the brand.
AmbientalPage.realidadeNotaAntes: They are all part of the
AmbientalPage.realidadeNotaDepois: portfolio, which also includes the MUB Garden, the first digital street furniture in Curitiba with a living garden, the Jardim Digital and the other pet squares in the city.
AmbientalPage.cicloTitulo: The life cycle of the vinyl
AmbientalPage.cicloH2: The vinyl comes off the face and comes back as a product.
AmbientalPage.cicloP1: Every printed campaign ends with vinyl taken down. The industry’s default destination is landfill. Ours is not.
AmbientalPage.cicloP2: Outdoormídia donates, at no cost, the advertising vinyl that has completed its display cycle. Trained seamstresses turn the material into tote bags and other products, generating income and taking waste out of circulation. A circular economy with a verifiable process, not a purchased seal.
AmbientalPage.cicloP3: The initiative is part of the Corajosamente Éticos programme, and all the proceeds go to a partner social project.
AmbientalPage.kopherTitulo: Donation of electronic waste to Instituto Kópher
AmbientalPage.kopherP1: We donated obsolete electronic equipment to Instituto Kópher, a non-profit organisation that has spent nine years promoting community wellbeing, combining environmental responsibility with social inclusion.
AmbientalPage.kopherP2: The donation directly supports the Programa Resgate, the institute’s pioneering initiative for the reverse manufacturing of electronic waste. The project trains people in vulnerable situations, especially in therapeutic communities, contributing to their reintegration into family and working life.
AmbientalPage.operacaoLead: A lit panel consumes energy and a printed face generates waste. Those are two bills outdoor media pays every month, and which our operation treats as a technical decision, not as talk.

GovernancaPage.lead: Approving an outdoor media purchase means knowing what licence the site operates under, what the contract says and who signs for it. In a privately held family company, that last answer has a first and last name.
GovernancaPage.ceoP1: Reputation in outdoor media is not built during the campaign. It is built **in what happens afterwards**.
GovernancaPage.ceoP2: This is **67 years of family operation**. The site installed today is still ours ten years from now, and so is the advertiser we serve. That changes how you negotiate, what you promise and what you refuse to do.
GovernancaPage.ceoP3: Halisson Pontarola is **CEO of Grupo Outdoormídia**, having led the company for **more than 30 years** and driven the transformation of the outdoor media sector in Brazil.
GovernancaPage.ceoP4: A business administrator, he holds an **MBA in Marketing** with an extension at **Penn State University**, a specialisation in Business Management from **FGV**, **Master Coach** training from SBC and a **master's degree in Theology**. His executive education also includes **Advanced Leadership** at the Haggai Institute, family business management at **EBC** and board member certification from **Fundação Dom Cabral**.
GovernancaPage.ceoP5: A speaker, mentor and adviser to business owners, he is the **founder of Mentoria 10+1**, where he works on developing leaders and entrepreneurs, focusing on resolving conflict in family corporate environments and on the sustainable growth of small and medium businesses. He is also the **author of the book Meu Pequeno Grande Negócio**, on strengthening management, leadership and business succession.
GovernancaPage.ceoP6: With **more than three decades of hands-on experience**, Halisson has built a leadership style marked by strategy, values and human development, helping family businesses evolve with **governance, clarity and a view of the future**.
GovernancaPage.ceoP7: He is currently also **President and Director of Central de Outdoor**, the national body that represents and develops the outdoor media market in Brazil.

SobrePage.lead: Nine outdoor media platforms across Paraná and Santa Catarina, operated end to end by our own team. From negotiation to installation, whoever promises is whoever delivers.
SobrePage.capaAlt: Aerial view of the Outdoormídia head office in Curitiba: the warehouses with solar panels and the branded façade
SobrePage.sobreOmP1: It all began in **1959**, along the highways of Paraná, with a bucket of glue, paper and an idea. Mr Euclides Aristides Farias was not selling outdoor media. He was pasting dreams onto paper panels, connecting messages to the movement of those crossing the roads.
SobrePage.sobreOmP2: Alongside his son-in-law, Hamilton Pontarola, he turned talent into vision and vision into a business. That is how **Outdoormídia** was born.
SobrePage.sobreOmP3: From a small family company in Curitiba, we became a benchmark for **Out of Home in Southern Brazil**. We grew by following the movement of the streets, the cities, the technology and, above all, the people.
SobrePage.sobreOmP4: That is 67 years and nine integrated **OOH and DOOH** platforms: the only operation in Paraná with that reach. From printed billboards to LED panels, we combine strategy, technology and audience intelligence to **place your brand where it needs to be seen**.
SobrePage.sobreOmP5: But that transformation did not happen on its own. It was built with every client who believed it could be done differently, and with a team that makes it happen every day, with **passion, craft and a view of the future**.
SobrePage.presencaTexto: We are present in Curitiba, the Metropolitan Region, the Paraná coast, Joinville, Itajaí and Balneário Camboriú, always at the sites with the highest flow, visibility and real impact.
SobrePage.compromissoLead: Occupying the street for 67 years creates an obligation towards it. What we do with waste, what we give back to the city and what we put in the contract.

compromisso.imageAlt: An Outdoormídia LED panel built into a vertical garden on a facade
compromisso.title: Environmental
compromisso.text: A lit panel uses energy and vinyl becomes waste. That is why we convert faces to LED, give the vinyl another destination and give back, in street furniture, what we take from the city.

compromisso.imageAlt: An Outdoormídia street furniture post with a 24h monitoring camera
compromisso.title: Social
compromisso.text: We are part of Corajosamente Éticos, we donate the vinyl that comes off the face so it becomes income at Loja OM do Bem, and we signed the first Regenerative Media asset in Curitiba.

compromisso.imageAlt: Portrait of Halisson Pontarola, CEO of Outdoormídia
compromisso.title: Governance
compromisso.text: An unlicensed site is a problem that splashes back onto the advertiser. All of ours are licensed, with exclusivity in the contract and a name answering for every line of it.

Culture.lead: We are the company that has been putting brands on the streets of Paraná and Santa Catarina since 1959. From printed billboards to LED panels, anyone joining the OM team works with the medium that has the greatest impact on urban centres.

pilares.title: The street is the product
pilares.text: Our media does not live in a browser tab. It is on the way home, on the highway, at the airport. Whoever works here sees the result of their own work out in the open.

pilares.title: 67 years, a market in motion
pilares.text: The company dates from 1959 and went digital: 175 digital screens, audience data per campaign and live cameras 24×7. The stability of a company that crossed six decades, with the technology of one that never stopped.

pilares.title: A lean team that owns what it does
pilares.text: From the negotiation to the installed site, whoever does it signs it. There are few layers between the idea and the street, and that counts for the client as much as for the people who work here.
